canonicalFindings.title: Unconfigured non-18-decimal token is silently treated as 18-dec 1:1 (fail-open default) — one forgotten setTokenConfig lets any NFT holder drain that strategy's full yield for ~0 payment, or bricks all claims
canonicalFindings.severityRationale: Both LLM scanners independently rated Medium: a C4 value-leak with a stated precondition (an owner config omission) rather than an unconditional High, BUT the impact magnitude on trigger is High (100% of a misconfigured <18-dec strategy's accrued yield, repeatable, silent/fail-open) and the symmetric variant is a full availability outage of the core function. This is the in-scope NON-OBVIOUS owner FOOTGUN (Law 3) that unknowingly enables a Law-1 value-extraction exploit — explicitly NOT the suppressed 'malicious owner drains' framing (C-01). FINAL SEVERITY TBD BY CLASSIFIER (Medium with a documented High-impact-on-trigger note to preserve per the conflicting-severity rule).
sourceAgentIds: SYMBOLIC-001 (halmos, payment>0 refuted on real bytecode)
PARK-LEDGER-01 (pattern manual-review, decimal-config mispricing footgun, profile PARK-01)
canonicalFindings.rootCause: Both _normalizeAmount (L586-609, fallback L591) and _denormalizeAmount (L617-640, fallback L622) treat an UNCONFIGURED token (tokenConfigs[token].decimals == 0 && normalizedExchangeRate == 0, the default struct state) as an 18-decimal, 1:1 passthrough (`return amount;`). Nothing links registration/funding to a required config: addYieldStrategy(strategy, token) (L227-236) takes no decimals argument and never requires a TokenConfig, and setRewardToken(_rewardToken) (L360-363) never requires a config for the new reward token. The decimal of a registered token is set in a SEPARATE, easy-to-forget owner call (setTokenConfig, L280-287). The fail-open default converts a benign owner omission into a silent value-conservation break.

canonicalFindings.bestDescription: claim() prices payment by normalizing each strategy's skimmed underlying to 18 decimals (L489 _normalizeAmount), summing, discounting (L497), then denormalizing to reward-token decimals (L498 _denormalizeAmount). If a registered strategy's underlying token (or the reward token) is left unconfigured while it is NOT actually 18-dec (e.g. 6-dec USDC/USDT), the 18-dec passthrough mis-scales value by 10**(18 - actualDecimals) (~1e12 for 6-dec stables). DRAIN DIRECTION (unconfigured strategy token): the skim loop delivers the FULL real underlying to the claimer (skimSurplus delivery is independent of SYA's pricing, L484), but totalNormalizedYield is understated ~1e12x, the discount math floors actualPayment to 0 (the L-01 floor, weaponized), minRewardTokenSupplied default 0 disables the only guard, and the claimer walks away with real yield for 0 reward token — repeatable, the only cost a burned NFT + gas, and a claimer can ISOLATE the misconfigured strategy via exemptStrategies (L473) to avoid paying for the correctly-configured ones. BRICK DIRECTION (unconfigured reward token): actualPayment is ~1e12x too large, safeTransferFrom (L509) reverts, and every yielding claim fails (fail-safe but a full outage) until the owner configures the token.
exploitPath: PRECONDITION (benign owner omission): owner calls addYieldStrategy(usdtStrategy, USDT) (L227) and configures the reward token correctly (setTokenConfig(USDC,6,1e18)) but forgets setTokenConfig(USDT,6,1e18). USDT stays (decimals==0, rate==0).
usdtStrategy accrues real yield, e.g. 1000 USDT (1000e6 native).
Any NFT holder calls claim(nftIndex, minRewardTokenSupplied=0, exemptStrategies=[all OTHER correctly-configured strategies]) to isolate the misconfigured one.
skimSurplus(USDT, claimer) delivers the full 1000e6 USDT to the claimer (L484) — real value received.
_normalizeAmount(1000e6, USDT) hits the unconfigured fallback (L591) and returns 1000e6 unscaled (treated as 18-dec) instead of 1000e18, so totalNormalizedYield is understated ~1e12x (L489).
claimerPayment = 1000e6 * (10000 - discount)/10000 ~= 9.8e8 (L497); actualPayment = _denormalizeAmount(9.8e8, USDC) divides by 10**(18-6)=1e12 (L634) => 0 (floors, L498).
actualPayment(0) >= minRewardTokenSupplied(0) passes (L501); nudge/phlimbo amounts 0 and skipped; safeTransferFrom(claimer, this, 0) succeeds (L509); no payment pulled.
Net: claimer receives 1000 USDT of real yield for 0 USDC. Repeatable every time the strategy accrues; phlimbo/Limbo stakers receive nothing for the (1-discount) share they were owed.
canonicalFindings.verification: PoC-confirmed via Tier-3 invariant (property-4 PAYMENT-FLOOR, encoded as the passing PoC test test_DecimalDrain_UnconfiguredStrategyToken_ZeroPayment in workspace/stable-yield-accumulator/test/PaymentFloor_SYA.t.sol: a 6-dec strategy token left unconfigured yields claimer 1000e6 real tokens while actualPayment==0 and phlimbo==0; the control test with the token configured charges the full 1000e6, proving the gap is the missing setTokenConfig) AND by halmos symbolic proof on REAL bytecode (SYMBOLIC-001 refutes 'payment>0' with a concrete counterexample via SYAHarness.exposedDenormalize; SYMBOLIC-002 PROVES the exact zero-payment region: actualPayment==0 <=> totalNormalizedYield*(10000-discountRate)/10000 < 10**(18-rewardTokenDecimals)). canonicalFindings.knownIssueDistinction: NOT covered by the 'decimal normalization to 18 (documented design)' known issue — that blesses the normalization MATH for CONFIGURED tokens; it does not bless (a) the silent (0,0)=>18-dec fallback masquerading as a valid config, nor (b) the absence of any link between addYieldStrategy/setRewardToken and a required TokenConfig. Distinct from C-01 (this needs no malicious owner — a single forgotten setter). The hazard is the missing enforcement, not the normalization formula.
canonicalFindings.recommendation: Make the unconfigured state FAIL-CLOSED, not fail-open. Any one closes the drain: (1) add an explicit `bool configured` to TokenConfig (set only by setTokenConfig) and revert in _normalizeAmount/_denormalizeAmount (or in claim) when a registered/reward token is unconfigured, instead of assuming 18-dec; (2) require tokenConfigs[token].decimals != 0 (or the configured flag) inside addYieldStrategy and setRewardToken; (3) fold decimals into addYieldStrategy's signature. Defense-in-depth: also revert when actualPayment == 0 for non-zero delivered yield (this hardens DEDUP-003/L-01 simultaneously). Document a deploy checklist: every strategy token AND the reward token MUST be configured before claims are enabled.
crossLinks: DEDUP-003 (ledger L-01): the standalone zero-payment floor is the MECHANISM this finding weaponizes ~1e12x. L-01 alone is dust-only Low and must NOT be re-escalated; this finding is the amplified, exploitable form. Keep both, cross-linked.
PARK-08 (rate==0 vs unset; a real 0-decimal token is indistinguishable from unconfigured) folds into this root cause — the proposed 'configured' flag also resolves PARK-08.

Surprise => footgun => IN SCOPE. Law 1 (no exploits) dominates Law 3 trust: machine-verified (invariant property-4 PoC + halmos SYMBOLIC-001/002 on real bytecode). canonicalFindings.title: setNudgeSplit(>0) does not require nudge != address(0) — enabling the split before wiring the recipient bricks every yielding claim (NudgeNotConfigured)
canonicalFindings.severityRationale: Permissionless core function (claim) is fully bricked for all yielding claims while the inconsistent (split>0, nudge==0) state holds, but it is owner-recoverable (set nudge or zero the split), causes no value loss, and the skim loop reverts atomically (no NFT consumed). C4 Low/QA availability footgun; non-obvious config-ordering hazard => in scope under Law 3. FINAL SEVERITY TBD BY CLASSIFIER.
canonicalFindings.rootCause: setNudgeSplit (L396-402) validates only `_split > 100` (InvalidNudgeSplit) and never checks nudge != address(0). The coupling invariant (split>0 requires a nudge address) is enforced only on the READ side — claim() L506 `if (nudgeSplit > 0 && nudge == address(0)) revert NudgeNotConfigured()` — so the contract permits entering the inconsistent state on the write side. (story-faithfulness confirms the L506 revert itself is INTENDED/documented in IStableYieldAccumulator L276-279; the gap is purely that the setter does not enforce it, leaving a non-obvious brick window.)

locations.role: only checks _split > 100; no nudge!=0 guard
allows clearing nudge to address(0) unconditionally (symmetric brick)
read-side revert NudgeNotConfigured after the skim loop (atomic rollback, no NFT burned)

canonicalFindings.bestDescription: If the owner calls setNudgeSplit(x>0) while nudge is still address(0) (or later clears nudge via setNudgeAddress(0) without zeroing the split), every claim with yield runs the skim loop and NFT-balance check, then reverts NudgeNotConfigured at L506 — atomically (no NFT consumed). The permissionless claim path (the contract's sole purpose) is fully bricked until the owner sets the nudge address or returns the split to 0. A competent owner enabling a new feature in the natural order (set the split, then wire the recipient) opens a brick window with no signal from the setter that the state is invalid.
exploitPath: Owner calls setNudgeSplit(20) intending to route 20% to a nudge recipient, before setNudgeAddress (L396 succeeds, no guard).
nudge is still address(0).
Any claim with yield runs the skim loop + NFT-balance check, then reverts NudgeNotConfigured at L506.
All yielding claims revert (atomically; NFTs not consumed) until the owner sets a valid nudge address or setNudgeSplit(0).
Same brick arises if the owner later setNudgeAddress(0) without first zeroing nudgeSplit.
canonicalFindings.verification: Static + manual reasoning (no machine PoC); root cause read directly from source (L396 vs L506). Both LLM scanners independently derived the same path; story-faithfulness corroborates the L506 revert is the documented intended behavior, confirming this is a write-side enforcement gap, not a behavioral bug.
canonicalFindings.recommendation: Enforce the invariant on the write side so the inconsistent state is unreachable: in setNudgeSplit, `if (_split > 0 && nudge == address(0)) revert NudgeNotConfigured();`; symmetrically in setNudgeAddress, reject clearing to address(0) while nudgeSplit > 0 (or auto-zero the split). This makes the L506 claim-time check defensive rather than load-bearing. Safe config order today: set the nudge ADDRESS first, then enable the split; to disable, zero the split before clearing the address.
canonicalFindings.consolidationNote: Three surfaces (CODE-002, ECON-02, PARK-LEDGER-03) are the same finding, same root cause, same location pair — one canonical Low footgun. NEW; not in the ledger.
canonicalFindings.sanitizerReason: SURVIVES. Not matched by any of the 8 known issues (none mention the nudge split). Root cause is a write-side enforcement gap: setNudgeSplit(>0) does not require nudge!=address(0), so the natural config order (enable split, then wire recipient) opens a window where every yielding claim reverts NudgeNotConfigured at the read-side check. Non-obvious config-ordering footgun (the setter gives no signal the state is invalid) => IN SCOPE under Law 3, not an 'obvious admin mistake'. Owner-recoverable availability hazard, atomic rollback (no NFT burned), no value loss. Final severity (Low/QA) deferred to classifier.

Correctly stays Low standalone. MUST NOT be re-escalated — only DEDUP-001 (misconfig) weaponizes it into a real drain. FINAL SEVERITY TBD BY CLASSIFIER (no change expected).

canonicalFindings.bestDescription: Under correct config the leak is <1 ulp of reward token per claim (dust, strictly unprofitable for the claimer once gas + NFT cost is counted). canonicalFindings.title: Phlimbo standing-allowance depletion bricks permissionless claim() until owner re-approves
canonicalFindings.severityRationale: Availability only, owner-recoverable, no value loss. C4 Low. FINAL SEVERITY TBD BY CLASSIFIER (no change expected).
canonicalFindings.rootCause: approvePhlimbo (L369-374) sets a fixed forceApprove allowance that the contract never tops up. claim() pulls phlimboAmount via IPhlimbo.collectReward at L519, which (verified at lib/.../phlimbo-ea/src/Phlimbo.sol:277, rewardToken.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, this, amount)) pulls EXACTLY `amount` against SYA's standing allowance — not a max allowance, not full balance. Cumulative pulls deplete the allowance; subsequent claims revert until the owner re-approves.

canonicalFindings.bestDescription: phlimbo PULLS its share via collectReward => transferFrom against a standing allowance the owner sets in approvePhlimbo. Once exhausted, EVERY claim reverts until the owner re-approves. nudgeSplit reduces the per-claim pull (phlimboAmount = actualPayment - nudgeAmount, L513) but does not change the depletion dynamic.

Claims accumulate; each pulls phlimboAmount via collectReward (L519), drawing down the standing allowance.
Once cumulative pulls exhaust the allowance, the next collectReward transferFrom reverts => claim() reverts.
Permissionless claims stay bricked until the owner re-approves.

canonicalFindings.title: Preview (snapshot estimate) diverges from charged amount (actual skim) with no payment ceiling; getTotalYield ignores per-token pause — no profitable sandwich
canonicalFindings.severityRationale: No protocol value loss and no third-party griefing: a claimer's payment always tracks the yield they actually receive, so they cannot be made to overpay relative to value received without also receiving that value (an attacker who inflates actualPayment by donating surplus also gifts the victim discount*donation — no profitable sandwich). Impact is claimer-side UX/self-DoS and unreliable bot quoting. C4 Low/QA. FINAL SEVERITY TBD BY CLASSIFIER.
sourceAgentIds: PATTERN-001 (pattern-db YIELD-PRINCIPAL-ACCOUNTING-SKEW / preview-vs-actual; down-weighted from potential-high)
PATTERN-006 (pattern-db MISSING-SLIPPAGE / no payment ceiling; down-weighted from potential-medium)
canonicalFindings.rootCauseClass: preview-vs-actual divergence / one-directional slippage guard / view inconsistency
canonicalFindings.rootCause: Previews (calculateClaimAmount L651, getYield, getTotalYield L738) price off the snapshot estimate _getYieldForStrategy = sum(totalBalanceOf - principalOf) over getAuthorizedClients(), while claim() prices off skimSurplus's post-redeem/post-swap underlyingReceived (L484). Per the vault CLAUDE.md these diverge (large in either direction for AMM-routed ERC4626 strategies). minRewardTokenSupplied (L501) is a FLOOR (min-yield proxy) with no MAX-payment ceiling; additionally getTotalYield (L738) does NOT skip tokenConfigs[token].paused whereas claim()/calculateClaimAmount() do, so the global view over-reports vs the claimable set. This two-source design is FAITHFUL/documented (story-025; _getYieldForStrategy NatSpec L542-547).

canonicalFindings.bestDescription: A claimer who pre-approves exactly the calculateClaimAmount quote can have claim() revert on safeTransferFrom when actual > preview (self-DoS, wasted gas; NFT preserved). Bots relying on getTotalYield can mis-size approvals/min because it counts paused tokens. No value leaves the protocol incorrectly — payment is always (1-discount)*value-of-delivered-yield under correct config. econ-scanner explicitly concluded NO profitable sandwich exists (an attacker cannot inflate the victim's actualPayment without also gifting the victim the corresponding yield), down-weighting the pattern-matcher's potential-high/medium framings.
canonicalFindings.verification: Static + economic reasoning. No exploit PoC (none warranted — no profitable adversarial path). code-scanner independently flagged the getTotalYield paused inconsistency as a QA view-layer observation.
canonicalFindings.recommendation: Add an optional maxRewardTokenSupplied ceiling to claim() (symmetric to the floor) so claimers can bound overpay; make getTotalYield skip paused tokens for consistency with claim()/calculateClaimAmount; document that calculateClaimAmount is an estimate and to buffer approvals.
canonicalFindings.consolidationNote: Three surfaces (ECON-03, PATTERN-001, PATTERN-006) collapse to ONE Low finding. PATTERN-001's clients[]-dedup / principal-skew angle has its root cause in the OOS strategy adapter (claim prices off the actual skimSurplus return, not the snapshot), so the in-scope slice is only the preview divergence — econ/code both class the strategy-side accounting OOS. NEW; not in ledger.
canonicalFindings.sanitizerReason: SURVIVES (in-scope slice). The strategy-side magnitude of preview-vs-actual divergence has its root in the OOS strategy adapter (lib/mutable/, KI#7) and the deduplicator already scoped that out; what remains is purely SYA-side and in-scope: (a) no max-payment ceiling on claim() (only a floor), (b) getTotalYield() omits the per-token paused skip that claim()/calculateClaimAmount() apply, so the global view over-reports vs the claimable set (a real SYA view inconsistency). econ-scanner concluded NO profitable sandwich (attacker inflating actualPayment also gifts the victim the yield). Low/QA per classifier; kept for recall.

canonicalFindings.title: Permissionless first-claimer captures the entire accumulated discount in one shot; minRewardTokenSupplied defaults to 0 (intended incentive + residual MEV note)
canonicalFindings.severityRationale: This is the INTENDED incentive mechanism: the discount exists precisely to pay whoever performs the decentralized conversion, and the protocol pays exactly discount*yield regardless of WHO claims, so there is no protocol value leak beyond the by-design incentive. The residual is ordinary MEV competition (gas auction among claimers) plus a foot-note that min=0 disables the per-claim floor. Informational/QA. FINAL SEVERITY TBD BY CLASSIFIER.
sourceAgentIds: PATTERN-007 (pattern-db BATCH-PAYOUT-FIXED-POT; nudge facet ruled a red herring, discount facet down-weighted from potential-medium)
canonicalFindings.rootCauseClass: MEV / first-claimer capture / default-disabled slippage guard (by-design)
canonicalFindings.rootCause: claim() skims ALL non-exempt strategies' surplus and applies the discount to the whole sum in a single permissionless call (L497). Accumulated yield is a growing pot; the first valid-NFT caller captures the full discount on it. minRewardTokenSupplied defaults to caller-chosen with 0 disabling the only floor. (PATTERN-007's nudge winner-take-all signature is a RED HERRING: nudge pays a PROPORTIONAL share to an OWNER-set recipient, L512, with no full-balance/count gate.)

locations.role: whole-pot discount applied in one permissionless call

canonicalFindings.bestDescription: No incremental protocol loss (discount is the budgeted incentive). Losers of the claim race revert with ZeroAmount (NFT preserved, gas wasted) — standard MEV race friction. A careless/bot claimer passing min=0 accepts any yield amount, including the dust/zero-payment edge (cross-ref DEDUP-003/L-01) — but that harms only the claimer's own economics, not the protocol. A searcher backrunning a large surplus accrual / a paused-token unpause and winning with a higher gas bid is the system working as designed.
canonicalFindings.verification: Economic reasoning. No exploit (explicitly down-weighted from the pattern's potential-medium; no sandwich exists — the first claim empties the pot, there is no shared post-loop balance to skim).
canonicalFindings.recommendation: None required for security. Optionally document the MEV/race expectation for integrators and recommend claim bots always pass a non-zero minRewardTokenSupplied derived from calculateClaimAmount (with a buffer) to avoid the dust/zero-payment edge.
canonicalFindings.consolidationNote: ECON-05 and PATTERN-007 collapse to ONE QA/informational item. The pattern's nudge winner-take-all match is documented as a non-issue (red herring). NEW; by-design. Ties min=0 exposure to DEDUP-003/L-01.
canonicalFindings.sanitizerReason: SURVIVES as QA/informational. The core 'first permissionless claimer captures the whole accumulated discount' IS the intended decentralized-conversion incentive (registry designDecisions[0]: 'Discount rate incentivizes external claimers to pay gas costs for conversion'); the protocol pays exactly discount*yield regardless of WHO claims, so there is no protocol value leak beyond the budgeted incentive and the claim-race is ordinary MEV working as designed. It is NOT in the formal 8 known-issues list, and it carries a small in-scope residual worth surfacing (minRewardTokenSupplied defaults to 0, disabling the per-claim floor; cross-linked to DEDUP-003/L-01). Per 'when in doubt, keep' + recall, passed to classifier where it will rank QA/informational rather than being silently dropped as by-design.

resolvedNotAFinding.title: divide-before-multiply in _denormalizeAmount (SLITHER-001 / PATTERN-002 over-charge facet)
resolvedNotAFinding.verdict: RESOLVED — not a standalone finding (refuted by code-scanner AND symbolic)
resolvedNotAFinding.reason: The literal divide-before-multiply ordering (divide by exchangeRate, then multiply by 10**(decimals-18)) lives EXCLUSIVELY in the decimals>18 branch of _denormalizeAmount (src L635-636), which is DEAD CODE: setTokenConfig reverts InvalidDecimals for decimals>18 (L282), so no configured token can reach it. On all reachable paths the down-scale is a single floor division (L634) that rounds in the claimer's favor by <1 ulp — that is exactly the DEDUP-003/L-01 floor surface, not a separate primitive. halmos SYMBOLIC-003 PROVED no over-charge (normalize(denormalize(y)) <= y) for the 6-dec 1:1 domain and confirmed the divide-before-multiply is confined to the dead branch (manualProofSupplement.deadCode). Kept visible per Law 1; the floor facet it shares with L-01 is carried in DEDUP-003.
resolvedNotAFinding.sanitizerReason: Already parked by deduplicator as not-a-finding (divide-before-multiply confined to DEAD decimals>18 branch; halmos SYMBOLIC-003 proved no over-charge). No known-issue/OOS action needed; does NOT proceed to classification. Floor facet it shares with L-01 is carried in DEDUP-003. Kept visible (Law 1).

resolvedNotAFinding.title: ERC777/CEI cross-function reentrancy via skim-then-pay delivery; ERC1155 burn-before-effects ordering (PATTERN-005 / PARK-LEDGER-04 reentrancy facets)
resolvedNotAFinding.reason: claim() is nonReentrant (OZ), so any ERC777-style tokensReceived hook firing during a skimSurplus delivery cannot re-enter claim(); every other state-mutating function is onlyOwner/onlyPauser, so a claimer-controlled callback has no SYA state to corrupt. The ERC1155 burn (L536) is a burn (no inbound receive hook) and precedes the skim loop, guarded by nonReentrant regardless; balanceOf>0 precedes burn; a later revert rolls back the burn atomically (no double-burn, no burn-on-zero-yield). The skim recipient is msg.sender, not arbitrary. NOTE: the doc/impl-mismatch facet of PATTERN-005 (skim-then-pay vs documented pay-then-skim) is NOT dropped — it is carried in DEDUP-005 (L-03). Only the reentrancy/exploit facet is resolved here.
resolvedNotAFinding.sanitizerReason: Already parked by deduplicator as not-exploitable (claim() is nonReentrant; all other state-mutators are onlyOwner/onlyPauser; ERC1155 burn has no inbound hook and rolls back atomically). No action needed; does NOT proceed to classification. The doc/impl-mismatch facet is carried in DEDUP-005/L-03. Kept visible.
